claims.text: The as-synthesized (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a large caloric response under applied magnetic-field and pressure-field operation.
The as-synthesized alloy has poor mechanical integrity and tends to crack.
Targeted heat treatment and/or micro-alloying can produce approximately 10–20 vol% multicomponent B2 precipitates in the target alloy.
The resulting B2 precipitates will form a coherent dispersion within the target-alloy matrix.
Ductile-transformable multicomponent B2 intermetallic precipitates can act as a strengthening phase in a high-entropy alloy.
B2 precipitates can undergo reversible martensitic transformation during cyclic deformation.
Reversible transformation of the B2 precipitates absorbs and dissipates strain energy during cyclic loading.
The B2 phase will delay fatigue-crack nucleation in the target alloy.
The B2 phase will delay crack propagation in the target alloy.
The B2 precipitates will not significantly interfere with the caloric phase transformation of the matrix.
The intervention will improve the target alloy's compressive strength.
The intervention will improve the target alloy's fatigue resistance.
Mechanical performance will improve by 25–50% relative to the untreated alloy.
The modified alloy will retain its caloric response within 5–10% of the untreated alloy's response.
Effectiveness requires tight control of precipitate volume fraction, morphology, and distribution.
Excessive precipitate content or improper processing may diminish the caloric response or introduce new mechanical degradation.
Operation must remain in temperature, magnetic-field, and pressure ranges that preserve the caloric phase and B2 precipitate stability.
